prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall state, and for its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B048 as my final position, and the exchange has made me more precise about why. Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 invariant and showed that a time-reversal-invariant band insulator can carry protected edge states without a magnetic field; Molenkamp's group then measured the predicted quantised helical edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells. About two decades of independent confirmation in transport, ARPES and other probes have made the interpretation stable, so the maturity question that hangs over B016 and the timing question that hangs over B049 do not arise here. Johansson, who opened with circuit QED, and Mehlig, who opened with hexatic melting, both moved to B048 after weighing the same record, which I take as evidence that the case survives scrutiny from outside the field and not only from my own ranking. I rest the case on the conceptual advance, a classification of electronic matter by topology beyond broken symmetry, and on the observation, and not on spintronics or topological quantum computing, which remain unrealised, as Olsson also urges.
statement.case_against: The attribution gap is real and the discussion has sharpened it. Pearce is right that Molenkamp's experiment was a direct test of the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal and not of the Kane-Mele graphene model, whose spin-orbit gap is far too small. Three names therefore cover a theory and an experiment connected through a fourth party, and the three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu, Kane and Mele; Moore and Balents; the ARPES discoveries) also lies outside. The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions and topological phases is neighbouring ground. Compared with B016, whose theory is the model its experiment tested, B048 has the weaker allocation, and compared with B049 it has the messier priority history. If the committee decides that the HgTe route requires crediting Bernevig, Hughes or Zhang, B048 cannot be repaired within three names and I would move to B016 or B049 and not patch it.

responses.point: Pearce argues that the maturity of B048 does not repair the BHZ gap, because Molenkamp tested BHZ and not Kane-Mele, so the credited theory and experiment do not connect directly; B016 has a direct chain from Bistritzer-MacDonald to Jarillo-Herrero.
responses.response: This is the strongest objection to my position and I accept its factual core: the HgTe experiment was designed around the BHZ proposal. Where I differ is on what the prize is for. BHZ identified the material and the band inversion that realises the Kane-Mele Z2 state, and Molenkamp's measurement was the first observation of that state, so the discovery being rewarded is the Z2 quantum spin Hall state and its observation, with the citation saying so and not claiming the whole route. That is a judgement about where the concept ends and the materials recipe begins, and I hold it with real uncertainty, since I am a non-specialist in condensed matter. I agree B016 has the tighter chain; my reason for not following Pearce is that B016 is seven years old and its superconducting mechanism is unsettled, which I weigh more heavily than a materials-proposal gap that a careful citation can state openly.

responses.point: Kroll asks whether a three-person split of B048 can be defended without Zhang, and says that if the citation is honest about the chain he would not oppose B048 as a second choice; he keeps B049 first on its clean Katori-Ye credit.
responses.response: My answer to his question is that I would defend it on the record only if the citation names the concept and the observation and nothing more. I would accept a wording such as 'for the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant Z2 topological insulator and quantum spin Hall state, and its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells', and I would regard a wording that credits the full HgTe prediction to Kane and Mele as disqualifying. I concede that B049 has the cleanest credit on the shortlist and that is why it is my second alternative. My remaining doubt is the one Kroll himself raises, whether lattice clocks are a new discovery or the best realisation within the toolkit honoured in 2005 and 2012. I cannot settle that from the ballots, and it is a question on which the atomic physicists, not I, should be pressed.

responses.point: Lindroth asks whether a citation can be drafted that is accurate about who predicted what in HgTe before B048 is treated as the clean option, and argues that the lattice clock changed the statistical regime and is a new idea and not a better trap.
responses.response: I withdraw the word clean for B048; it has a clean arc and an unclean allocation, and the chair's question asks us to say so. The wording above is my attempt to answer her request, and it is accurate in saying that Kane and Mele predicted the Z2 state and Molenkamp's group observed it, while leaving BHZ's specific HgTe prediction unstated and therefore uncredited. I find her argument on magic-wavelength trapping persuasive as physics: removing the differential light shift so that many atoms can be interrogated at once is an insight and not engineering. It moves B049 closer to B048 in my assessment than it was in round 1. It does not move it ahead, because Kroll and she both rely on recalled history for Katori's priority, while the B048 priority problem is at least identified and bounded.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B016 on a direct theory-to-experiment link and judges the existence of the correlated insulators and superconductivity reproduced, but says he would not resist B048 strongly, as it is the safer choice on maturity.
responses.response: I appreciate that he distinguishes the established phenomena from the open mechanism, and I agree that the discovery of correlated states in twisted bilayer graphene is reproduced and not in doubt. We therefore disagree only about weighting. A prize can reward a reproduced phenomenon without a settled mechanism, and I do not treat the open pairing question as disqualifying. But the field is still moving quickly, the credited experimental names leave out Cao and the 2018 team, and I would rather the committee wait a few years than award a platform whose definition is still being written. If he and Pearce can show that the Cao co-first-author issue is handled by the three-name limit as routinely as claimed, I would take B016 seriously as the better configuration, and I keep it as my first alternative for that reason.

responses.point: Mehlig, who moved to B048, says the citation should rest on the Z2 prediction and HgTe observation, that the graphene gap means the prediction was for a model, and that B016 is the cleaner triple if the attribution is judged unresolvable.
responses.response: I agree with him on all three points and I regard his conditional as the right test for the vote: if a member concludes that BHZ is essential to the discovery, then B016 is the honest alternative and not a patched B048. I would add that his observation about the graphene gap is why Molenkamp's role is not a supporting one; without the HgTe observation Kane and Mele's work would remain a model. His own concern about the 2016 overlap I share only in part, because time-reversal-invariant Z2 matter without a magnetic field is a different regime from the quantum Hall topology and defect-driven transitions recognised in 2016, but I accept that it counts as a cost when we weigh a second topology prize.

uncertainties: Whether the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal is better understood as a bridge between the Kane-Mele concept and the observation, as I have argued, or as an essential step in the discovery, which would make three names unsound. This is a judgement about priority that I make from recalled history in a field that is not mine.
Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases is close enough to weigh against B048 beyond what I have allowed.

Whether seven years of confirmation for B016 should count as sufficient given the open pairing mechanism, since Pearce and Eriksson treat the phenomenon as established while I give more weight to the unsettled mechanism and the Cao co-first-author problem.
Whether lattice clocks (B049) are a distinct discovery after the 2005 and 2012 prizes; I cannot resolve this from the supplied record and Katori's priority rests partly on recalled history.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on B048, B016 or B049 is apparent from my profile, and I do not revise my round 1 disclosure. My documented connections are David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theoretical-physics group, none of whom is credited on the shortlist. Eriksson's disclosure concerns Uppsala electronic-structure theory and B006, which I am not supporting, and I note it only as a colleague connection at my own institution, not a candidate-related tie. My own field is string theory and cosmology, so I am a non-specialist in condensed matter and atomic physics, and I weigh attribution claims accordingly.
